reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace R, MeasurableSpace and BorelSpace instances and canonical Lebesgue volume; dimension zero is allowed. Let V:E->R, alpha,beta:NNReal and eta:R. Assume alpha cast to R is strictly positive, alpha<=beta, V is C2, and for every x,v in E,
  alpha*||v||^2 <= (fderiv R (fderiv R V) x v) v <= beta*||v||^2.
Assume eta>0 and beta*eta<=1. Define the actual measures and potential
  mu=volume.tilted(x->-V(x)),
  J=map((x,g)->(x,x+sqrt(eta)*g), mu.prod(stdGaussian E)),
  W_y(z)=V((y+z)/2)+||z-y||^2/(8*eta).
The tilt of -F has density exp(-F)/integral exp(-F) against volume; nonzero normalization is not built into the definition. The Gaussian is the standard real Hilbert Gaussian, the product is independent, and map is actual pushforward.
There exist kernels R,S:E->Measure E such that R and S are Markov kernels, R is a conditional kernel disintegrating J.map Prod.swap, and for every y in E,
  S(y)=(R(y)).map(x->2*x-y).
For every y in E, S(y)=volume.tilted(z->-W_y(z)), W_y is C2, exp(-W_y) is Lebesgue integrable, and its Lebesgue integral is strictly positive. For this y there exists a real-linear partial operator D:L2(S(y);R)->L2(S(y);E) with dense domain in the actual scalar L2 space, with D closable and D.closure closed, and with exactly this graph: for every a in scalar L2(S(y)) and H in vector L2(S(y)), (a,H) belongs to graph(D) if and only if there exists a smooth compactly supported phi:E->R with a=phi S(y)-almost everywhere and H=gradient(phi) S(y)-almost everywhere.
For every real epsilon>0 and every scalar L2 input f for this same D, there exists u in domain(D.closure) satisfying the following simultaneous conclusions. Write u_rep and f_rep for the standard measurable representatives of the actual scalar L2 classes, and G_rep for the standard representative of G=D.closure(u) in the actual vector L2 quotient. In the formulas below set r(x)=epsilon*u_rep(x)+<gradient(W_y)(x),G_rep(x)>_E-f_rep(x); this notation abbreviates the exact displayed expression.
(1) For every v in domain(D.closure),
  epsilon*<u,v>_{L2(S(y);R)}+<D.closure(u),D.closure(v)>_{L2(S(y);E)}=<f,v>_{L2(S(y);R)}.
(2) u_rep and G_rep are locally integrable with respect to canonical Lebesgue volume.
(3) For every C1 compactly supported psi:E->R and every direction v in E, both x->psi(x)*<G_rep(x),v>_E and x->u_rep(x)*(fderiv R psi x v) are Lebesgue integrable, and
  integral psi(x)*<G_rep(x),v>_E dx = - integral u_rep(x)*(fderiv R psi x v) dx.
(4) x->||r(x)||^2 is locally Lebesgue integrable, with the real scalar norm in this squared expression.
(5) For every compact set K contained in E, u_rep, G_rep, and r each satisfy MemLp with exponent 2 and the actual restricted measure volume.restrict K. Each assertion includes a.e. strong measurability and finite L2 norm with respect to that restricted measure.
(6) For every C2 compactly supported phi:E->R, both x->u_rep(x)*Laplacian.laplacian(phi)(x) and x->r(x)*phi(x) are Lebesgue integrable, and
  integral u_rep(x)*Laplacian.laplacian(phi)(x) dx = integral r(x)*phi(x) dx.
Here the test-function Laplacian is the actual finite-basis trace of its derivative. The distribution equation tests u_rep against this C2 test Laplacian; it makes no pointwise total-Laplacian assertion about u_rep. The Hilbert variational inner products use S(y), while all local integrability and distribution integrals use canonical Lebesgue volume. One u and its actual output G serve all variational v, all C1 directional tests, every compact K, and all C2 distribution tests.
One pair R,S works for every y. For each y one D is chosen before every positive epsilon and every L2 input f, and the same D works for all of them; it is not chosen anew for each epsilon or f. The density and operator conclusions hold for all y, not merely almost every y. The conditional-kernel property itself has the usual disintegration scope and does not make a claim about every possible version on exceptional y. The exact r is epsilon*u_rep+<gradient(W_y),G_rep>-f_rep. No classical Laplacian or H2 conclusion for u, core theorem, measurable y-dependent operator/solution selection, kernel invariance, or quantitative solution bound is asserted.
objects: Global C2 potential V, NNReal alpha,beta, real eta; normalized Gibbs tilt mu, actual independent standard Gaussian product and noisy joint pushforward J; midpoint-quadratic W_y; actual Markov R,S with swapped-joint disintegration and reflection map; for each y a densely defined closable scalar-to-vector L2(S y) partial gradient D with closed closure; positive epsilon, arbitrary scalar L2 forcing f, selected u/G and residual r; ordinary weak-gradient and Laplacian distribution tests and compact-volume L2 restrictions.
domains: E is finite-dimensional real inner-product and Borel, including dimension zero, with canonical volume. Scalar and vector Lp classes at exponent 2 are the actual quotient spaces and their coercions are the standard measurable representatives. D is a real-linear partial operator with a submodule domain; u and the variational v are elements of D.closure.domain; G=D.closure u lies in the actual vector L2 quotient. All local integrability, unannotated Integrable and integral expressions use volume. All compact restrictions explicitly use volume.restrict K. Ordinary directional v lies in E. C1/C2 test functions are real valued and compact topological support; graph generators are smooth compactly supported. Laplacian.laplacian phi is the actual finite-basis trace on the C2 test phi, not a Laplacian applied to arbitrary L2 u. For each y both L2 quotients and Hilbert inner products use S y. mu=volume.tilted(-V); J is the pushforward of mu.prod(stdGaussian E) under (x,g)->(x,x+sqrt(eta)*g); W_y(z)=V((y+z)/2)+||z-y||^2/(8*eta). Kernels are measurable probability transition families by the asserted Markov properties.
quantifiers: Universally over displayed E instances, V, NNReal alpha,beta and real eta satisfying all premises; Hessian bounds hold forall x,v:E. After lets mu,J,W, exists one pair R,S; reflection identity forall y; the potential-density/regularity/positive-partition/operator/solution block forall y. For each y exists one D before forall epsilon:R, epsilon>0 -> forall f:scalar L2(S y). The exact graph property is forall a,H with exists smooth compact-support graph generator. For each epsilon,f exists one u before forall closure-domain variational v, forall C1 compact-support psi and all directions v:E, forall compact K, and forall C2 compact-support phi. D is fiberwise fixed across all epsilon and forcing, and u is fixed across every test and compact restriction.
assumptions: NormedAddCommGroup E, InnerProductSpace R E, FiniteDimensional R E, MeasurableSpace E, BorelSpace E and canonical volume; V:E->R, alpha,beta:NNReal, eta:R; alpha cast strictly positive; alpha<=beta; V C2; for every x,v both alpha*||v||^2 <= (fderiv R (fderiv R V) x v) v and that diagonal second derivative <= beta*||v||^2; eta>0 and beta*eta<=1. Positivity/integrability for W_y, dense-domain D, closability, closed closure and exact graph are conclusions, not additional premises. epsilon>0 is an inner antecedent; f is unrestricted within actual scalar L2(S y).
conclusion: Exists R,S both Markov, with R a true conditional kernel for J.map Prod.swap and S y=(R y).map(x->2*x-y) for every y. For every y, S y equals the normalized volume tilt of -W_y, W_y is C2, exp(-W_y) is volume-integrable with positive volume integral; exists D with dense domain, closability, closed closure and graph exactly smooth compact-support scalar/gradient classes modulo S y. For every positive epsilon and every actual scalar L2 f, exists one u in closure-domain satisfying all: universal Hilbert variational equation; local volume integrability of scalar u_rep and vector G_rep; for every C1 compact-support psi and v:E both ordinary weak-gradient products are volume-integrable and integral psi*<G_rep,v>=-integral u_rep*Dpsi[v]; local volume integrability of ||r||^2; for every compact K all three actual MemLp 2 (volume.restrict K) assertions for u_rep,G_rep,r; for every C2 compact-support phi both u_rep*Laplacian(phi) and r*phi are volume-integrable and their integrals are equal. r is exactly epsilon*u_rep+<gradient of the stated potential,G_rep>-f_rep. All use the same selected u and actual G, not independently chosen representative outputs. Here r uses gradient(W y).
scopes: One chosen R,S pair serves all y; R disintegrates the actual swapped noisy joint (Y,X), not an abstract pair of unrelated marginal measures. W_y uses exact midpoint and quadratic penalty. All y have the density identity and a D; one D per y serves every positive epsilon and L2 forcing f. Actual quotient representatives of u,G,f occur in r and the volume conclusions. No assertion about every conditional-kernel version on all y or a jointly measurable y->D/u selection. The final ordinary equation is unweighted volume integral u*Delta(phi)=integral r*phi; no pointwise total Delta u, H2 or core theorem, covariance/invariance/iteration result, quantitative bound, uniqueness, or separate mu probability-measure conjunct.
constant_dependencies: alpha>0, beta>=alpha are NNReal; eta>0 and beta*eta<=1 retained exactly. Joint noise coefficient sqrt(eta), reflection coefficient 2, midpoint coefficient 1/2, and penalty denominator 8*eta. No unspecified numerical constant. mu depends on V; J on mu,eta and standard Gaussian; W_y on V,eta,y. R,S may depend on outer data, D on y and S y; u on y,D,epsilon,f. G=closureD(u); r exact epsilon*u+<gradient W_y,G>-f. epsilon any positive real, exponent exactly 2, tests/K universal after u.
